newsitem.title: UK: IGC raises 1997/98 world wheat trade by 1 mln T.
newsitem.headline: IGC raises 1997/98 world wheat trade by 1 mln T.

text.p: The International Grains Council on Thursday revised its estimate for 1997-98 world wheat trade up to 94 million tonnes from 93 million estimated last month.
In its latest Grains Market Report, the IGC also put 1996-97 trade at 93 million tonnes.
Much of the latest increase came from rises in estimated imports by countries in Africa. Egypt's imports were forecast at 6.5 million tonnes, compared with the previous estimate of 6.2 million.
Morrocco's imports were put at 2.5 million tonnes, up from a previous estimate of 2.2 million.
The IGC put the rise in north African imports down to the sharp decline in regional harvests.
South Africa's estimated imports were revised up to 600,000 tonnes compared with the previous figure of 500,000.

On the other side of the trade equation, the IGC revised its figure for 1997-98 Canadian exports down to 19.5 million tonnes from the previous 20 million, as a result of Canada's lower than earlier expected production. --Christopher Lyddon, London newsroom +44 171 542 7928
